notes: The title is COMMENTS ON "PURSUING STACKS". The sheet contains eleven correction entries, seven before and four after the heading Section 14 etc.

The p3 comment lists three numbered advantages of simplicial sets: cartesian closure, the realisation equivalence for Kan simplicial sets and CW-spaces, and compatibility of realisation with products with the stated topology qualification. Entry 3 continues with literature, Dold-Kan, and a reference to a simplicial proof by A. Dress in the unnamed author's paper with Heath, "Cogluing homotopy equivalences".
The last paragraph contrasts cubical sets, mentions Massey and Brown-Higgins, and stops after "not firmly embedded in the". Its continuation is not supplied from elsewhere.
The source gives no author name, date, typed page number, or page-count statement on this sheet. The visible 12 is the archive corner number.

math_checks.outcome: Checked entry 1 directly as a presheaf construction: define (Y^X)_n = Hom_sSet(Delta[n] x X, Y), with simplicial operators by precomposition. A map Z x X -> Y restricts along each simplex Delta[n] -> Z to a compatible element of (Y^X)_n, and evaluation reverses this construction. The two constructions are inverse, giving the required exponential adjunction. This supports the all-simplicial-sets claim; no change to its wording is needed.

Checked the scope of the unqualified words chain complexes by the grading of normalized chains: N_n(A) is formed from A_n for n >= 0, and there are no negative simplicial degrees. Thus the usual normalization statement presupposes a nonnegative grading convention; the sentence itself does not supply that qualification. The half visibly reads only chain complexes, which is preserved. This is a grading/scope check, not a new proof of Dold-Kan.
